canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether a long-term human liver tissue chip can characterize rifampicin-mediated regulation of hepatic transporters and drug-metabolizing enzymes using matched mRNA, protein, functional CYP activity, bile-acid, and intracellular rifampicin measurements.
Long-term liver tissue chips were established with primary human hepatocytes from three individual donors (ZTZ/Donor 1, ZYW/Donor 2, and WID/Donor 3).

population.label: Primary human hepatocytes from three individual donors

canonical_statement: CYP activity studies were conducted with Donors 2 and 3; Donor 1 was not used for the CYP activity cocktail because CYP2D6 protein was undetectable and the donor had a CYP2D6 polymorphism.
Beginning on culture day 3, rifampicin-treated chips received 10 µM rifampicin with daily spiking for 7 days.

exposures.details: Added starting on culture day 3 and spiked daily through the 7-day treatment period.

canonical_statement: Vehicle-control chips received 0.1% DMSO during the same treatment period.

exposures.details: 0.1% DMSO vehicle control.

canonical_statement: Liver tissue chips were seeded with 215,000 primary human hepatocytes per chamber on collagen I/fibronectin-coated chambers, overlaid with Matrigel, and maintained under recirculating flow at 2 mL/hour.
mRNA abundance was measured by RT-qPCR using the ΔΔCt method with beta-actin as the reference gene.
Transporter and drug-metabolizing-enzyme protein concentrations were measured by targeted absolute proteomics on membrane-enriched fractions.
CYP activities in Donors 2 and 3 were assessed with a five-probe cocktail (midazolam, diclofenac, R-omeprazole, tacrine, and dextromethorphan) followed by LC-MS/MS measurement of probe metabolites.
Six extracellular bile-acid species (GCA, GCDCA, GCDCA-3G, GCDCA-S, TCA, and TCDCA) were profiled from daily media samples by LC-MS/MS.
After 7 days of rifampicin treatment, intracellular rifampicin was quantified and unbound intracellular concentration was estimated using a reported intracellular unbound fraction of 0.0096.
Statistical comparisons used multiple two-sided unpaired t-tests with Holm-Sidak correction in GraphPad Prism 10.6.1.
By culture day 10, albumin production in rifampicin-treated Donor 1 chips was reduced by approximately 47% relative to DMSO controls.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that transporter-protein induction by rifampicin was modest relative to CYP induction, with transporter proteins reaching at most about 2.7-fold while CYP protein induction reached 32.9-fold in the tested liver tissue chips.

The authors characterized this study as an initial demonstration that the liver tissue chip can support integrated assessment of inducer effects, and proposed the platform as a foundation for future new-approach-method qualification rather than a completed clinical induction-risk predictor.
Only one rifampicin concentration was evaluated, so concentration–response parameters such as Emax and IndC50 could not be determined.
Only one prototypical inducer was evaluated, limiting extrapolation to other nuclear-receptor agonists or inducing drugs.
The study did not perform in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation or physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling to test clinical DDI prediction.
Transporter activity was not directly measured, so protein changes cannot by themselves establish functional transporter induction.
